title: Tight Security for 3-Round KACs with Identical Key Schedules
summary: Good-key analysis is resolved for the stated sub-key independence level, but bounding bad keys to prove tight security for 3-round KACs with identical key schedules remains open.

formal_statement.body: For key-alternating ciphers (KACs), the good-key analysis has been resolved for sub-keys satisfying $p^{t-2q}$-wise independence. The unresolved problem is to develop a new method for bounding the bad keys and thereby prove tight security for 3-round KACs whose sub-keys use identical key schedules. The task is to establish this tight-security result under the identical-schedule condition, with $p^{t-2q}$-wise independent sub-keys as the stated baseline.

scope.domain: Tight-security analysis of 3-round key-alternating block ciphers whose sub-keys use identical key schedules.
assumptions: Sub-keys satisfy $p^{t-2q}$-wise independence as the stated baseline.
parameters: $p^{t-2q}$-wise independence: baseline independence level for the sub-keys
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop new bad-key bounds and use them to prove tight security for 3-round KACs with identical key schedules.

progress.summary: The source reports the good-key analysis as resolved for $p^{t-2q}$-wise independent sub-keys and identifies bad-key bounding as the missing step toward tight security for identical-schedule 3-round KACs.
citation_labels: Stefano Tessaro et al., Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys
